Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Call recap:
- FinSecure is evaluating an LLM-powered assistant for support/claims workflows; the data touched will include customer PII and transaction records.
- Primary concerns: data isolation (preventing cross-tenant access to logs/requests), customer-managed encryption (KMS), and auditability (retention of request logs and ability to export).
- You flagged potential regulatory constraints that may require on-prem or a VPC-only deployment for certain workloads.

Clarifying questions (to confirm fit):
1) Which data classes will be sent to the model for the PoC? (e.g., hashed identifiers vs raw PII vs full transaction payloads)
2) Is it acceptable for model weights and shared model artifacts to be hosted in a shared environment if inference requests and logs remain isolated?
3) Do you require customer-managed KMS for all encryption-at-rest keys, or only for exported artifacts/archives?
4) Any mandatory network controls (PrivateLink, egress restrictions, no internet egress) or paperwork (3rd-party attestation) we should include in the MAD?

What I recommend next:
- If you need logical separation (isolated tenancy for requests, no cross-tenant KV/log access) and customer KMS, Redwood Dedicated is usually sufficient and gives predictable throughput.
- If you require physical isolation (no shared hosts for inference, or air-gapped/offline), Private (VPC or on-prem) is the path — we can scope an on-prem pilot.

I attached our deployment options brief for a quick side-by-side. If you can reply with answers to Q1–Q4, I’ll loop in rishi (cc’d) to draft a recommended MAD and sample SOW.

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up next week with Rishi for architecture details — what days/time work for you?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Answering your questions inline: 

1) Data classes: For the PoC we'll send hashed customer IDs and full transaction payloads (transaction descriptions). We will NOT send unredacted SSNs or payment card numbers.
2) Model weights: hosting model weights in a shared environment is fine as long as inference requests, logs, and cache remain logically isolated per tenant and never land in shared persistent logs.
3) KMS: We require customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption of stored logs and any exported datasets. For ephemeral in-memory caches, customer KMS is preferred but not mandatory for the PoC.
4) Network controls: PrivateLink or VPN with no public egress for production. For the PoC, a dedicated VPC peering + strict egress rules is acceptable. We will need SOC 2 Type II and network diagram before showing to our security/compliance team.

One more question: Does Redwood Dedicated guarantee that inference runs on dedicated GPUs (no co-located tenants)? Or is that only Private on-prem/Dedicated pools with physical isolation?

I've attached a short requirements spreadsheet for our security team.

—Alex

Alex — thanks for the fast responses and the spreadsheet (received). A few clarifications and a proposed MAD attached: 

- Dedicated vs Private: 
  - Redwood Dedicated: provides tenant-level isolation for request routing, KV/prefix caching isolation, and isolated logging per customer. Dedicated uses reserved GPU pools assigned to your account — those are not shared with other customers. However, the underlying hardware may be in the same data center/rack as other customers unless you contract an on-prem or fully isolated Private pool. Dedicated gives equivalent logical isolation and SLA-backed throughput we typically recommend for production unless your compliance team requires fully private hardware.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, ability to run in your VPC or on your premises, and options for customer-managed KMS/HSM and strict egress controls. This is the path when your compliance policy requires no co-located tenant hardware.

- KMS and logs: we support customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest and can restrict log retention/export workflows. For the PoC we can enable KMS for stored artifacts and provide a limited retention/export policy for your evaluation.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to set up a technical follow-up (30–45 minutes) to go over network setup and KMS integration (Rishi — can you take this?)
2) I’ll upload SOC 2 summary and a sample network diagram to the shared drive and send to your security team.
3) If PoC looks good, draft MAD and SOW/scope (attached) and route for internal approvals.

Alex — are you available Tue/Wed next week for the technical call? If you confirm, I’ll send an invite (Rishi on the call).

Best,
Marissa
